A truly great horror game experience that whilst it made use of jump scares, did not rely on them. An engaging story of horror, with a cast of sick and twisted individuals to torment and terrify you.
Set in an insane asylum run by a nefarious group, you play an intrepid reporter, intent on getting a great stroy. Unfortunately for you, it turns out that you are to become that great story, and your aims quickly change to a simpler one: Get Out!
There is a mix of supernatural and pseudo science that has an X-Files feeling to it but at its heart this game is a classic horror experience. You don't fight, you run and you hide. Actually the hide mechanics are pretty good and the 'enemy' AI will keep you on your toes (or cowering under a bed). And the game uses an interesting mechanic in the nightvision mode of the camera. It allowed the game to cover you in darkness and yet still be able to see, albeit not very well, and having to use valuable batteries. But more importantly it somehow made the game feel more real. More like a documentary gone wrong. Something akin to the Blair Witch Project.
If you like horror games, this is a must have.

I rate this game 3/5. The game’s OK I guess though I’m really not that good at it.
Pros: This game has many different difficulty levels and AI tactical settings allowing for a great deal of replayability, There are two campaigns and a skirmish/simulated multiplayer mode in addition to actual multiplayer possibilities, the graphics are the best I have seen on any RTS tactical game other asides from the Homeworld games and yet the system requirements are relatively low. The game also runs fast. There are 3 playable factions to choose from, the music is adequate at worst and catchy at best, the sound is outstanding, the controls have an easy learning curve and work well. This is definitely a worthy successor to the previous primary command and conquer game (Tiberium Sun) and picks up the story where that game left off. Units and structures are interesting and yet easy to identify (particularly if you are familiar with this kind of game), the game appears to be completely free of any bugs, the game's menus and interfaces are fine and yet for all this...
Cons: This game is extremely difficult for a variety of reasons (and therein lies its main failing (or is it mine?). The AI on any setting rated medium or over can be extremely unforgiving of any tactical mistakes (as it appears to make no mistakes itself), the realism and realistic importance of the "tactics" involved in playing this game are questionable at best (and totally nonsensical at worst) as the game almost continually appears to encourage you to take 100 percent losses and attack without having all of your people and vehicles in order (or even constructed). Coordination between different types of vehicles and soldiers is a necessity but such vital elements such as airstrikes and artillery are given an odd, back-seat to the main, ground-based action (which is actually classic, normal gameplay for the Command and Conquer franchise). Air power is stronger in this iteration of the game than in previous Command and Conquer games but is still quite weak, requiring 4 or more aircraft of any type to have much of an affect in any battle (as was still true in past CC games)
For all of the game's futuristic appearances, units behave in an oddly World War II styled manner (with similar (or lesser) ranges applying to their weaponry (as was also shown in past CC games), the game still often manages to feel like an elaborate board game throughout (like its predecessors), the environments are interesting and often beautiful but fall under only 3 main categories (alien, war-ravaged desert, and cityscape with some greenery), The main campaigns become extremely frustrating very quickly as they begin to continually (to the extent that the game becomes extremely predictable) place you in situations wherein the enemy has a totally unfair advantage and your own forces are in a state of severe disarray (as in previous CC games).
The skirmish maps are perhaps the most fun part of the game but there is unfortunately not a great variety of them and they are often setup in an overly formal manner (it ends up looking sort of like you are having a battle in a war-ravaged formal french garden further adding to the feeling that you are playing a complicated board game). Perhaps the worst part of all this is however, how much raw potential for fun and interest which the game has but doesn't manage to live up to. The tactics in this tactical game rarely make much real-world sense....Or maybe I'm simply not very good at it or the tactical situations may simply be too nonsensical even for my tastes (but I never can seem to gather enough resources fast enough no matter how many refineries I build and regardless of where on the battlefield I build them).
A friend of mine who tends to play more strategy/tactical games than I do also once told me he was having a hard time with this game too though...so maybe it's just a really, really hard game.
Kane’s Wrath is better in every respect. It’s too bad you have to install this to play Kane’s Wrath.

Blood and Bacon is a simple game that was made for fun, so that friends could get together and just have some fun blowing up giant pigs. There isn't much more than that. But is this game a bloody mess, or does it really bring home the bacon?
Story: You and/or a couple of your friends are trapped at a farm in a barn along with The Farmer, who is nailed to the wall with a pitchfork. He's actually pretty funny, and his monotone voice works with that really well. He has a ton of guns and ammo in the barn for you to go out each day and destroy the demon pigs that have taken over his farm. That's really it. This game doesn't have or need much story. You go outside and blow up pigs. It's goofy and it works really well.
Presentation: This is an indie game that is incredibly stupid and thats what makes it great. The graphics are very meh and the games physics actually work pretty good for what it wants to be. It has a huge Left 4 Dead feel and it works great. The presentation is not the best, but it isn't supposed to be, and it works really great for what it is.
Gameplay: The game itself is very fun to put it short. Expecially with friends, which is what the game was made for. Each day there is a number of pigs outside on the farm, and your goal is to destroy them all. It's super bloody and bits of pig go everywhere. On the farm there are water pumps that heal you, and electric fence you can activate to fry pigs, and a huge meat grinder, that you can push pigs into to get grenades, ammo, etc. There are a few secrets to find as well. Like I said earlier, the game is very L4D, so you have a primary and secondary you can grab from the barn each day, unlocking more every so often for more pure carnitage (I had to). If you run out of health, you fall down into last stand mode where a friend must pick you up. It's silly, bloody, and really fun to play with a friend or three.
Blood and Bacon is really fun, gory, and humorous as well. It's only a dollar, so definatly buy a copy, and gift a few to some friends. It's a quick and super fun mulitplayer game for a few friends to play around in.

Jet Gunner tries to be like Contra without understanding what made Contra actually so great. Contra was well made all around, with specific enemy placement, gameplay tweaks and generally a sense of design, that always kept things fair for the player. If you died, you always had that feeling, that it was your mistake and you can do better next time. Jet Gunner unfortunately doesn't offer this. Enemies shoot you right in the face, before you can even see them properly, the controls are incredibly awkward and the level design doesn't even try to compensate for that.
For example, since enemies are so relentless you end up shooting all the time. Simultaneously the level design asks of you to use your Jetpack in certain areas which have enemies. So you are trying to control the finicky jetpack with one button, while at the same time trying to fire. Get hit one time and you get propelled backwards without mercy and usually end up in a pit, resulting in instant death. It's quirks like this, that make Jet Gunner not really enjoyable.
It's a pity, since it looks kind of good and works as a game. With a bit more care it could have been much better, but as it is, it is nigh unplayable. That music is very annoying doesn't help either. :/

There are only two buttons for both running & jumping, the D-pad for movement, and a pause button. Both KB+M and a controller are viable but you can't rebind anything; instead, you get one of those "control/keyboard scheme 1, 2, 3" kind of settings.
The aspect ratio of the game is on 4:3 and going into window mode sets the resolution to something less than 480p, so the game can look incredibly small if played that way. As far as I'm aware, there's no regular means to change that and you don't even get any resolution options, just fullscreen and window.
The graphics & music are indeed 8-bit. The graphics leave much to be desired in actual detail; there are even some times when you can mistake the background for a wall or a platform. The music, while not very special but isn't horrible either, loop terribly enough that you can hear where it cuts off to repeat the current song.
The gameplay's as simplistic as it makes itself out to be; run-and-gun from one side of the map to the next. You even get an automatically recharging jetpack that keeps you in the air for as long as you keep pressing the jump button and the meter has "fuel", which is also pretty nicely used for progressing through the levels. There are somewhat carefully placed health pick-ups as well as lives in almost every map, giving you infinite lives in a sense since every pick-up respawns. Losing all lives means you have to restart the current stage from the start.
Each stage has their own unique theme and, excluding the final stage, each one has two mini-bosses and one end-boss; all fairly easy once learned, save for one stage whose map just leaves far too little room to move around in.
It's a pretty difficult game overall, though not exactly in a good way.
Weapon pick-ups are placed in set places but what kind they'll be is completely random. They're fairly varied in what type they are, however most are worse than the rest. The pick-ups are also random as there's a good chance you'll pick up something that will be more hindering than useful for the situation, at least if you don't know what their image symbols mean, so you're encouraged to learn them in case you may come across something that doesn't even shoot straight ahead when you really need something that shoots straight ahead. Even worse, you can only have one type of weapon at a time.
When enemies capable of ranged attacks come on screen, they often fire fast shots as soon as they become visible, punishing you as a result for running at all. Even if you've got the fastest reaction time out of anyone ever, the shots are just simply faster than you can avoid. The only effective way of staying truly safe from that is knowing beforehand what's coming as you run or move pixel by pixel to stay safe. I think that these problems even exist to begin with is because the player character is set right in the middle of the screen as he moves along, making enemies appear faster than they probably should. The bosses don't have this problem as their entire maps are just the one screen you immediately see as you transition to their map.
There's a Challenge Mode that unlocks a set of challenges for every stage cleared. They're alright as they're really just extra stages to clear with a predetermined setting, like "one shot death" and "beat the timer". The challenges involving the jetpack are broken though; they'll say something like "jetpack disabled", but it isn't.
A Hardcore mode is available from the start which removes health/lives pick-ups, the jetpack depletes faster, your defense is decreased, and boss health is increased. It can be a major difficulty spike when you jump in from either Normal Mode or Challenge Mode. In some maps, it can become a complete mess of frustration for a variety of reasons until you figure out the sure-fire ways of getting through the obstacles with little to no damage.
The base game probably won't even take a few hours to beat. This is my second japanese game, after playing Learn Japanese To Survive! Katakana Battle. I'm glad I played that one first, because I don't think I would have given it a shot if this was my introduction to the series.
There's too many frustrations to enjoy the experience. On the learning side, the "how to draw" segments are painfully ambigious for some characters, making it hard to tell when a stroke is actually connected. I wish they would show us the font's rendering of the character during these segments, so that I can tell how to *actually* draw it. Additionally, vocabulary is almost always "here's the word, next" rather than any reinforcement learning.
The gameplay itself, though, is painful. Without a lot - a lot! - of grinding, basic encounters will shred your party. This makes for a very frustrating gameplay loop. I wasn't actually able to finish the game; I got to a point where there was a gauntlet of encounters without healing between, and I couldn't pass it without committing to a lot of grinding. I did cover the entire alphabet before tapping out. The encounter rate is very high, and the map design requires a lot of back-and-forthing, making combats a nuisance. Eventually I just started running from most of them, which probably contributed to my under-poweredness. Enemy encounters were frustratingly non-varied; most areas seem to have only two different sets of enemies, rarely going back to earlier characters.
I recommend this series' Katakana battle, but you're probably better off learning Hiragana somewhere else.

There's something to be said about games that just make you feel happy.
A Hat in Time isn't perfect by any means, but it's a hopelessly cute and absurdly fun, with all the blemishes and unpolished bits being few and far between. The game borrows heavily from a lot of 1996-2005 3D Platformer games era, you'll draw comparisons from the obvious Super Mario 64 and Sunshine (main suspects) to the more obscure Sly Cooper and Pyschonauts games. Every chapter is structured completely different from one another, which eases the feel of repetition but might throw others in for a loop. One Chapter you'll be on an little happy greek-esque sunny island, and few dairy entries later you'll be in a surreal spooky forest under a dark and gloomy moonlit sky with somber melancholy undertones. A lot of the characters you'll encounter are brimming with personality with a few particular characters standing out more than others but with an overall a very humble and tight knit cast of creatures and friends for you meet and play with. And this soundtrack is one for the ages... You get a vast arrangement styles of music. Did anyone mention the Grandpapa of Whimsical Adventure OSTs Grant Kirkhope makes an appearance in some of these tracks?
Overall A Hat in Time is an awesome game that restores faith to the 3D platformer genre and draws faithful and quirky twists to old classic games from the yesteryear. It's a game that I'd recommend to anyone who is interested in playing for a laid back, play at your once pace, hecka adorbs space adventure.

It reminds me of my favorite 3D platformers like Spyro and Psychonauts. It's nice to see a great new game like those. The controls aren't quite *perfectly* tight in this game, so I sometimes felt out of control, though it was still very good. It feels good to be able to go very far and fast by applying skill; in fact, I wish that there were more racing maps. The game is fairly easy overall, but there are challenging bits. It does a good job at avoiding being *frustratingly* difficult.
The maps are highly varied and interesting. Some are very large. The collect-a-thon was a bit weak, though. You'd almost have to go out of your way *not* to get the required yarn, and there aren't enough relics to pose much of a challenege. I 100%ed the game in about 18 hours. The hat mechanic was fine, but it seems underused; I didn't change hats or badges all that often. I kinda feel like they could've doubled the length of the game just by exploiting existing content/features more, without reducing overall quality. Maybe the upcoming user-created maps feature will sort of provide this.
The story and models are super cute. I love the different hats flairs and colors. The story is interesting, with lively and memorable characters. I like how Hat Girl comes across as devious, if benevolent -- it's a bit different than usual.
The music is excellent, and perfectly complements what's going on in the game. I love how as you advance in a level, often the music will flow into a different flavor of the same general song.

I bought this on day one for the art style and animation. While I wasn't entirely disappointed, I did find one glaring flaw; not everything looks 100% traditionally animated. Some assets, enemies, and obstacles will smoothly slide around the screen, looking distinctly cheap when compared to the consistantly beautiful traditional animation. The woodpecker in the tree level, for example, will have one frozen frame glide into view, then start animating for its attack, and then freeze again to glide away. That's ugly.
This isn't a humongous gripe, given how amazing most of the game looks, but it is a detraction that I cannot overlook.
The gameplay itself is simple and old school. Imagine Contra, but with a couple more ideas, like air-dashing and parrying. I wouldn't call the gameplay amazing, but it's very solid.
If you like rubber hose animation and difficult action games, buy this now. Even with its flaws, it's worth it.

Good quality jump-scares are the name of the game.  You know what you're getting within ten minutes of play; don't expect a nuanced psychological thriller, it's not even particularly well-written outside of the entertaining babbling of the various loonies, but it looks and sounds good, it's PACKED with GORE and entertaining SHOCK moments that even knocked me out of my seat a few times.
You can expect 7-8 hours of play time for your money, and I don't think my nerves or attention span would have lasted much longer.
PRO: Good visuals, well above the usual indie quality, pretty great sound and voice acting, at least one particularly memorable character, pointed little tributes to other horror games and films, game is just long enough to not overstay its welcome.  Some really nice attention to detail sometimes.  Genuinely good jumps-scares.  Baddies with weens.
CON: Very little variation in enemy, gameplay or so-called puzzle design,  Tone-breaking and weak attempts at humour in the not-so-well-written textual content.  Almost immediately starts with piles of gore, making you rather quickly numbed to seeing entrails, severed heads etc.  The 'note' system encourages you to use the video camera almost always - even when not dark - which is sadly rendered with a headache-inducing video effect.
In conclusion, very adequate fun and lots of cute shocks, though I suspect the game's repetition means not much replay value.  Looking forward to Outlast 2.

I picked this one up last week and frankly I can't get enough of it. I'm a big fan of survival titles, and this one does it quite well. It's selling point is the atmosphere it creates. Everything from the wind wistling in rafters of an unheated cabin, to blazing sunrises to the pure confusion and terorr of getting caught in a blizzard in the middle of the night.
In it's current state, you can only play in sandbox mode, so there is no story yet. But that doesn't make it any less playable. It's interesting to see how many days you can get through, surviving wolf attacks, making sure you have enough food/water, trying to explore the surroundings, and of course, trying not to freeze to death ( which can be a sirious challenge at times ).

I ended up enjoying the game and finishing it, but there's a mile long list of issues with this game. Combat is fun and appropriately balanced on higher difficulties. AI companions vary between being excellent (good at healing you, dodging, comboing, etc.) and being as dumb as a brick. There are occacionally camera issues, but this usually doesn't make the combat any less fun. The weakest aspect of the game is easily the story, which is, to put it politely, a sack of hot garbage. Fortunately, you are never given much of an oppurtunity to get invested so you can approach the plot the same way you might approach a so-bad-it's-good movie. Character quality varies. Some are funny snark machines (I credit one such snark machine for getting me though much of the game), others are hyper bland, while others are downright insufferable.  Character interactions in the skits are fun though. As a rule, Zestiria is fun as long as you aren't taking it seriously. Give everyone a silly costume, laugh at the cliches and the skits and the snark, and don't think about any plot point too hard and you'll have a good time.

Jet gunner successfully carves out its own identity in the crowded genre of retro inspired platformers. Some may be quick to make the Mega Man comparison, but it's clearly a lot more Contra crossed with Shatterhand with its own twists added in, namely the titular jetpack. The hovering controls feel very fluid and give you a wide range of movement options, though waiting for the jetpack to recharge was occasionally annoying, especially when the buddy bots only stick around for a limited time. Though there are a few poorly designed sections that stick out, the design of the enemies and level mechanics overall is clever and very well thought out. The weapon variety is nice, especially when considering the many combinations of guns and buddy bots, although some weapons are certainly lacking and feel bad to play with, namely the ones that limit your fire rate. The visual aesthetic is very nice, with colors that absolutely pop, though certain foreground elements looked like background elements and vise versa. The audio design is a bit hit or miss; the music is good, if a bit understated, but certain weapons don't have the impactful sound effects they deserve. All in all, Jet Gunner is a fun experience, if a bit short and occasionally rough around the edges. I'd certainly recommend it for the given price.

This is my first tales game, and I played it to completion, but it felt like a chore after a while.  I believe this is because the world design has significant issues in terms of backtracking or constantly turning off the save point travel system.  That and what typically drives me in any RPG game is a compelling storyline and character development that has me wanting to keep playing to see what happens or to make decisions that affect the world I'm playing in.  In this case the character development is poor, the story is linear, and there are few if any decisions you can make to affect the world.  The main character is pretty much the same person at the beginning as he is at the end, and the dialogue is often painfully corny or nonsensical.
You can tell the game tries to have these large shock value or impactful moments with the death of a character or a reveal of an aspect of their past, but the game never first creates the connection that would make you care for the characters.  So these moments fall flat, and are laughable at times.   It's not a terrible game by any means, but just not worth your time.  That is unless you are a long time tales fan or perhaps catch it at an extreme discount when you have nothing else to play.

TL;DR can be worth it if you can get it for cheap(~5$ or in a bundle).
Although enjoyable, the game is riddled with various flaws:
-  a cross between 2D and 3D controls which the "tale of" series should never have adopted. either is fine but the mix has killed the serie for me. I had hope for this 1 since it seemed full 3D fight but it still force a forced aim lock on enemies which somewhat remind 2D controls.
- no control on the camera during fight. The camera stay still when you dodge which make it really confusing.
- the crafting system doesn't offer enough freedom. It wouldn't be too much of a problem if it wasn't of the overly complex passive skill system.
- the passive system is interesting but it's quite complex and the game menu make it impossible to work with it. I gave up trying until I'm much further in the game.
- All the combat system feel pointless when it really matter. What really matter is just your stats. To give an exemple I'm fighting one of the "region boss". so far they've been ~10levels higher than monsters in the area. Given its high level it pretty 1shot me if I dont block or dodge. The issue is that even when blocking I still take too much damage and if I dodge the enemy chain attacks so fast that it attack a second time while I'm still dodging the first attack. If I instead go on offensive and chain attack the boss will randomly become invincible for no apparent reason. He sometimes do it as soon the fight begin and sometimes after I manage to combo him down to 25% of his HP.
- given the unfair nature of the combat system you can almost consider fighting alone. AI fail to do anything interesting except sometimes keeping your combo alive between 2 chains. Spellcasters will get taken down immediatly  as they draw a lot of aggro and all monsters will flock on them in a second. Forget about stopping them they just move too fast.
I do want to complete the game, or at least go far enough to unveil more of the plot. The game do try (akwardly) to keep some surprise for later in the game. It's enough to keep me engaged but it's nothing special enough for me to say you're missing on something if you dont play.

Tales of Zestiria adalah salah satu dari 15 JRPG dari seri "Tales" yang di rilis oleh Bandai Namco, game ini memiliki gameplay yang penuh aksi, terutama dalam scene battle. Pada seri terbarunya ini, Tales of Zestiria memiliki sistem battle yang lebih rumit dan memerlukan taktik, terutama ketika melawan musuh dengan kekuatan besar, misalnya Boss di suatu Dungeon. Cukup banyak yang perlu dipelajari, bahkan kita dapat menemukan pelajaran mengenai sistem battle yang diselipkan ke dalam "Skits!" - (Otaku pasti ngerti).
Pada Tales of Zestiria, Bandai Namco menampilkan cerita yang begitu apik, baik dari sisi kedalaman ceritanya maupun humor yang terkandung di dalamnya. Bagi penggemar setia seri Tales, sentilan percakapan pendek jenaka yang biasanya muncul dalam mini event, atau disebut juga dengan Skits dalam seri game ini, adalah resep paling jitu untuk menjaga gamer betah seharian di depan layar. Selain untuk menghilangkan kejenuhan, Skits juga memperlihatkan emosi yang berkembang di antara setiap karakternya. Hal ini juga masih terlihat begitu kental dan terjaga dalam Tales of Zestiria.
Meskipun ceritanya terlihat sederhana, tetapi game ini memperlihatkan alur cerita yang begitu dalam dan menarik. Apa yang terlihat tidak selalu demikian adanya. Begitu juga dengan kenyataan bahwa ada saja pihak manusia yang berusaha untuk menguasai kekuatan Shepherd demi keuntungannya sendiri, meskipun dengan risiko kehancuran dunia. Semua itu dinarasikan dengan sangat baik dalam beragam percakapan, Skits, dan event. Menariknya, game ini memberikan akses kepada Anda untuk menggunakan aktor suara asli dari versi Jepang.

Using this game, I learned all the hiragana in 7 hours with a little bit of supplementary practice on the side. To help you with your studies, I've provided some additional links at the very bottom of this review!
This game is amazing for people who need a little push in learning hiragana. It teaches you a set of hiragana at a time and makes you fight "Hiragana Warriors" with their sound. For example, you will see "あ" and fight it with "a." There are certain segments of the game that reverses this and makes you fight "a" with "あ," but unfortunately, you cannot revisit those sections--they're a one-time event.
The biggest downside to this game is that you cannot use this game to practice all the hiragana it teaches you, While you can revisit areas of the game and fight the same "blocks" they assigned, they never toss all the hiragana together outside of boss battles that you cannot revisit--hence why I'm about to link you to outside practice. The downside that you don't see when you don't practice all the hiragana together is that there are several hiragana that can easily be confused that are never presented together, so you might never realize it's a problem unless your practice.
HELPFUL LINKS:
- Having trouble memorizing some hiragana?
has a mnemonic based learning system that can help you supplement what you're learning in game!
- As I mentioned earlier, the game does very little to prepare you for
, so make sure you look over this and practice identifying among them.
-
has recently come out and is great for that extra practice.
- Practice as much as you can! Quizlet has many resources. You can likely search "Hiragana" on your phone's app store and come up with some nice on the go practice. With a week of decent practice, you'll do great!!

Pretty decent visual novel. Its not that good, but it isnt bad either.
You are a farmer which leaves his house and failed crops in order to investigate plague that is spread across the land. Story was pretty interesting and mysterious at start, and later on it builds up to a searching game where you'll look for items to progress through story. However, i wish it explained little more about the end of the story, as it feels like something is missing.
I like how the game lets you explore the parts which will kill you, for example trying to fight a bear with small rocks. Each unique death also rewards you with achievement which makes them even more interesting to find.
Pros:
- Unique black and white art, which fits well with creepy story
- Story isnt that bad, and was pretty mysterious at start
- Easy to 100%
- Low system requirements
- Alot of save slots (more than 10 but i dont think you'll need that many)
Neutral:
- Although its a visual novel, it would be interesting if instead of clicking the sentences we could click on objects we want to interact with. However this does would require more development.
- It could use some puzzles to do along the way to make it little more interesting
Cons:
- Even though story is nice, i would like if it had more backstory

Super Hot is a (currently) new Indie Game.
The Main Goal of the Game is simple, clear the Level.
But the twist is the Unique Mechanic the Game brings.
"Time only moves, when you move".
The Game Executes the Mechanic pretty good.
The only Problem i have is that the Guns (Espacilly the Pistol), feel very Slugish.
That also makes it look like your just holding the weapon, instead of waiting for the recoil to wear off.
At the End of each Stage you also see a replay in "Normal speed".
I say that because, its basically just your Gameplay Speeded up which let it sometimes look weird.
The Game is also REALLY short just about 2 hours of the ingame story,
you can literally refund it.
2 hours is kind of a joke, considering in the current state the game cost ~20€/$.
So whats good and why should you buy it anyway?
well first up:
the game has alot of cool things.
The most see able is the Death Physiks of the"Red Guys"
They literally scatter like broken diamonds on the floor.
Then because of the time only moves wh... yeah whatever you can do things like, catch a katana that you throw to yourself with the new mechanic. (Yes its really not just the demo that we all played a year ago).
The new mechanic work like this:
Every ~10 ingame seconds you can travel into the body of an enemy,
with the side effect that,
first: that enemy will drop their gun,
second: the body you were in turns into an enemy.
You will find yourself using that mechanic to get out of unavoidable situations or to travel to another part of the Stage
CONCLUSION:
In the end the game is a very cool/very fun game to play,
its just overpriced.
Luckily its not just the demo we played already.
MY SUGESTION:
wait until the game gets a 50% sale.
Considering theres nothing big to add into the game,
this should soon happen.

There's something to be said about games that just make you feel happy.
A Hat in Time isn't perfect by any means, but it's a hopelessly cute and absurdly fun, with all the blemishes and unpolished bits being few and far between. The game borrows heavily from a lot of 1996-2005 3D Platformer games era, you'll draw comparisons from the obvious Super Mario 64 and Sunshine (main suspects) to the more obscure Sly Cooper and Pyschonauts games. Every chapter is structured completely different from one another, which eases the feel of repetition but might throw others in for a loop. One Chapter you'll be on an little happy greek-esque sunny island, and few dairy entries later you'll be in a surreal spooky forest under a dark and gloomy moonlit sky with somber melancholy undertones. A lot of the characters you'll encounter are brimming with personality with a few particular characters standing out more than others but with an overall a very humble and tight knit cast of creatures and friends for you meet and play with. And this soundtrack is one for the ages... You get a vast arrangement styles of music. Did anyone mention the Grandpapa of Whimsical Adventure OSTs Grant Kirkhope makes an appearance in some of these tracks?
Overall A Hat in Time is an awesome game that restores faith to the 3D platformer genre and draws faithful and quirky twists to old classic games from the yesteryear. It's a game that I'd recommend to anyone who is interested in playing for a laid back, play at your once pace, hecka adorbs space adventure.

So I played this game for ~11 hours in the past 3 days and I never make reviews so here's the deal.
-
By buying the green resource you can pretty much obtain everything in the game. From constructing buildings on your planet faster, to unlocking guild EXP (yes, you can unlock EXP with real money) to scrolls to upgrade your abilities to make them stronger (yes, you can make your abilities stronger with REAL money).
-
yes, bots. You play in the ranked ladder with and/or against bots. you can get 2 bots in your team versus a full human player team. These are not third party bots, these are bots that are actually put into the game to make it appear as if people play this game and the queue times would not go further than 30 seconds.
-
Sloppy. even some part of the character's mesh glitches out because I think the bones weren't attached correctly.
-
Not only do you constantly play with/against bots that often result in you having to 1v3, you can only rank up ONCE each monday. from bronze 3 to bronze 2 each for example, only each monday if you are in the top 10. I had 1200 score on top 1 of my 20-person leaderboard (with #2 only having ~300) and I was promoted to bronze 2.
-
Making your own planet and attack other player's planets, putting together your army to attack and defend. Guild exp and individual guild member exp. 3 different PvP (let's not forget that every game has 80% bots) modes.
To me it feels like a few people just wanted to quickly whip up a game to earn some money. Game can be fun for 5-10 hours, at least for me, but then the bots and endless grind starts to kick in. You can't climb in this game too as you have to wait 1 week to be promoted.

It reminds me of my favorite 3D platformers like Spyro and Psychonauts. It's nice to see a great new game like those. The controls aren't quite *perfectly* tight in this game, so I sometimes felt out of control, though it was still very good. It feels good to be able to go very far and fast by applying skill; in fact, I wish that there were more racing maps. The game is fairly easy overall, but there are challenging bits. It does a good job at avoiding being *frustratingly* difficult.
The maps are highly varied and interesting. Some are very large. The collect-a-thon was a bit weak, though. You'd almost have to go out of your way *not* to get the required yarn, and there aren't enough relics to pose much of a challenege. I 100%ed the game in about 18 hours. The hat mechanic was fine, but it seems underused; I didn't change hats or badges all that often. I kinda feel like they could've doubled the length of the game just by exploiting existing content/features more, without reducing overall quality. Maybe the upcoming user-created maps feature will sort of provide this.
The story and models are super cute. I love the different hats flairs and colors. The story is interesting, with lively and memorable characters. I like how Hat Girl comes across as devious, if benevolent -- it's a bit different than usual.
The music is excellent, and perfectly complements what's going on in the game. I love how as you advance in a level, often the music will flow into a different flavor of the same general song.
9.5/10, highly recommended to anyone who likes old-school 3D platformers.

A truly great horror game experience that whilst it made use of jump scares, did not rely on them. An engaging story of horror, with a cast of sick and twisted individuals to torment and terrify you.
Set in an insane asylum run by a nefarious group, you play an intrepid reporter, intent on getting a great stroy. Unfortunately for you, it turns out that you are to become that great story, and your aims quickly change to a simpler one: Get Out!
There is a mix of supernatural and pseudo science that has an X-Files feeling to it but at its heart this game is a classic horror experience. You don't fight, you run and you hide. Actually the hide mechanics are pretty good and the 'enemy' AI will keep you on your toes (or cowering under a bed). And the game uses an interesting mechanic in the nightvision mode of the camera. It allowed the game to cover you in darkness and yet still be able to see, albeit not very well, and having to use valuable batteries. But more importantly it somehow made the game feel more real. More like a documentary gone wrong. Something akin to the Blair Witch Project.
If you like horror games, this is a must have.

Gameplay- 9.5/10
The gamplay is just fantastic and fun. There is a good variety of bosses, and the run and gun stages are very fun and hectic, too. The reason I didn't give it a solid 10 is because the game is about learning from your mistakes and playing the stage over and over until you perfect it. I myself like this type of difficulty, becuase the game forces you to git gud. You feel your skills improving, and i love that. Though, I understand the trial and error isn't for everybody, and might discourage some people.
Graphics- 15/10
Cuphead is easily one of the most unique and beautiful looking indie games that came out possibly ever. The 1940's Fleischer animation style is just filled to the brim with charm and creativity. The bosses and enemies are designed very creatively, and I can't wait for to see how the bosses will look later in the game. The graphics kept me smiling even after all those deaths I suffered. The game is so loyal to the style, that it really feels like you're playing through a cartoon straight from the 40's.
Sound- 11/10
The sound is equally as authentic and loyal to the era as the graphics are. The music is a lot of upbeat jazz that's just really nice to listen to. I especially love the title screen song. The sound effects are very 1940's-esque aswell. It's made by human mouths, and i just love it.
Difficulty and Fairness- 10/10
The difficulty is just excellent. The game doesn't hold your hand, but it's not ball-bustingly impossible, either. There is a lot of trial and error, but I like this because like i said before, the game forces you to improve and get better. Sure, you CAN buy items and weapons that'll make your life a little easier from the shop, but the game is still very much based on skill, not luck or items. This makes finally making it to the end of a level, or landing the final blow on a boss all the more satifiying, especially if you were struggling.
Overall 11/10
Cuphead is an excellent indie game that was completely worth the wait and delays. I implore you to buy this game if you're a fan of games like Contra or Mega man, if you're a fan of animation, or even if you're just curious. Cuphead is a gem that's worth every penny, and I'm eagerly waiting to see what StudioMDHR has in store next.

PROS :
1) No glitches / crashes at all that I have noticed.  Not A One.
2) Easy interface system to learn.
3) Daunting, hostile weather conditions.
4) Visibility limitations that make sense.
5) Interesting fatigue/food/water system affects overall condition in ways that make sense.
6) Some crafting & use of available resources.
7) Good use of sound, nice visual imagery, fluid feel of play.
8) Impending sense of danger. Quick changes in weather & predator situations require your attention.
9) Appreciation for the 'safe moments', holed up in a cabin with a good fire going, hot food & drink while the wind howls outside.
10) Wolves.  Lots and lots of wolves.  Sneaky, devious, crafty wolves ....
11) Three different difficulty settings to choose from.
12) Good dev interaction on the forums.
CONS:
1) Needs more crafting & available resource options still.
2) No ability to make spears ... yet ... ?  I continue to hold out hope :)
3) Combat takes some getting used to (game autoselects your best weapon).
4) Act of survival can get rather repetitive / monotonous if you hole up in one area.
5) Some actions (ex. fishing) seem more work than they are worth.

The good news is that even in its current state this game is playable, but that doesn't necessarily translate to actually being enjoyable. Let me be perfectly blunt if you are looking for a decent or even somewhat realistic simulation. This game isn't for you, or at least it isn't the game for you yet. If you are looking for a deeply satisfying game experience this probably isn't the game for you either at least not yet. The game as it is right now is just tedious, and frankly while there is potential. The real question is potential for what. It is really hard to see the end of the road on this title, because of all the conflicting choices present in the build.
The gameplay basically amounts to rinse and repeat. You basically loot an environment, consume all of the resources that are available to you, and then move on to the next area to repeat the process. While being shackled by mechanics that drag the whole affair out. There is no character development, and no actual hard won knowledge. You just go from one building to another looting containers, and stopping every few rooms to make more room in your spartan inventory. Often having to wait for a number of minutes as you use the resources you have acquired to feed a furnace. Even as far as sandboxes go this game is incredibly light on endgame. As the goal is to see how long you can last before you die.
The obstacles placed before you aren't so much inspired as they are just cheap. A awful inventory system that compels you to carry dead weight. Dogs and Wolves that throw you into quick time events, and white outs that force you to just sit and wait with nothing to do while you wait. It wouldn't be so bad if the world were inviting, but it isn't really. Setting aside the fact that it is a barren wasteland. There isn't any whimsy, flavor, or proffered scenarios to give you something to do. It is just moving from one house to the next to loot. There is no sense of discovery, strategy, or skill. I cannot in good conscience recommend this game.
The skeleton is there to be seen, but there just isn't any meat on the bones. I think the game has potential it just isn't to a point where it is both playable and enjoyable. The world just isn't dynamic enough to keep your attention, and as far as the simulation aspects are concerned they aren't actually all that good. Largely due to the attempt to create any kind of gaming experience. So there just isn't anything on offer yet.  I would recommend waiting until this game has much more to offer. Wait until real decision making elements are introduced, and a story, and scenarios.

This was wonderful. I just finished the game a little bit ago, and I've already purchased Katakana War. I was using Duolingo on my phone, but honestly, this game had me learning and speaking Japanese much faster. I can highly recommend this game for anyone wanting to learn the basics to Japanese. + Makes learning Hiragana simple
+ Battle system is easy to understand and gives much nostalgia to anyone who played JRPGs in the 90's

All together, I'd give this game a 9/10. Great for learning, fun to play, and the story is simple but isn't boring by any means. Ready to see what happens next and learn Katakana on the way!

First of all for anyone who is starting to learn japanese, Go for the order Hiragana-Katakana-Kanji (Hiragana First).
second, This Game should take you from 15-20 gameplay hours depending on your focus level ( I took like 17.5).

Side Quests give the game extra fun and more multi-tasking and finishing all of them will get you a reward ;)
After you finish this game "immediately" you should be able to:
1- Remember minimum 40 Hiragana (46 Total)
2-Read Hiragana (slowly but surely!)
3-Write Hiragana(not perfectly but surely!)
4-Understand very little basic Grammar notes
5-Know at least 10 japanese words (if you focus truly you can know like a 70!)
Drawbacks:
1-Game shouldn't cost more than 5$, my problem is that i live in Egypt where 1 dollar = 18.5 pounds so 2 dollars cause a huge difference
2-Combat can get boring especially when you get the same exact scenario twice in a row(3 times once!)
3-Some Maps will have Combat Encounters every 3 sec which sucks if you want to avoid them because you insured that you remember the Hiragana
4-Some Places on the world map aren't meant to be visited and will always be locked which can turn off the player after he finishes the game
5-Glitch where if you go to the ship (Won't Spoil) manually as of to the place you find it first at you will turn to a ghost
6-No AutoSaving System (Not really a problem unless you forget) BUT THEY REMIND YOU SO FORGET THIS ONE
7-You Can't Skip lessons when you review them which sucks when you forget like 1 of the symbols from a set
8-Can't customize players which isn't really a problem to be honest.
IF YOU WANT TO LEARN HIRAGANA, BUY THIS AND DON'T HESITATE!!!!!

Jet Gunner é um jogo de plataformas em 2D ao estilo de Contra e Megaman, grandes clássicos da NES. Este jogo tem como objetivo fazer relembrar os velhos tempos da NES e na minha opinião, acho que cumpre bem o seu papel. Não é nada de extraordinário, temos 6 níveis para completarmos com dificuldade á nossa escolha e temos um conjunto de Challenges para quem quiser entreter-se mais com o jogo. A qualidade de gráficos, aúdio e jogabilidade está tudo no ponto e o desafio não falta, especialmente nas partes finais(vá se foder a força da gravidade). Para o preço que é, acho que vale muitíssimo a pena e para quem quer experimentar um pouco do que é o "Retro Gaming", este é um jogo indicado para si! ;)
English:
Jet Gunner is a 2D side-scroller reminding me of Contra and Megaman, big classics on the NES. This game aims to remind us the good old times of the NES and in my opinion, it does the job well. There´s nothing extraordinary here, we´ve got 6 levels to beat(with difficulty of our choosing) and we have a set of challenges for anyone who wants to spend more time in the game. The graphics, the sound and the gameplay quality are all fine and the challenge is great, especially in the last levels(♥♥♥♥ gravity). Given the price, I think it´s very worth and for anyone who wants to taste a little bit of the "Retro Gaming Spirit", this is the game for you! ;)

First Impression: Jet Gunner is..alright. It captures the look and feel of a NES run and gunner graphically and soundtrack wise, and the idea of a limited backpack with a variety of weapons sound like a potential idea for something like a sequel to Power Blade 2. The problem is that running and gunning will get you killed even though it is a "run and gunner". Standard ground enemies will shoot the moment they appear on screen and their bullets are very quick - so instead of playing the game "Contra" style where you should either kill the enemy quick or jump over the slow moving bullet, you should step carefully and "bait the enemy into shooting" so you can then jump the projectile and try to kill them.
Some powerups feel alot worse than the standard auto rifle - a slow firing, slow moving shockwave, a somewhat homing giant boomerange with only two projectiles at a time, innacurate missiles. Some weapons are clearly better than others, and unlike Contra, the weapons that spawn are random, so you can't optimize your playthrough for the best weapon.
I also found some enemy and trap placement a bit cheap. This is probably a way to "make the game classic Nintendo" hard," but this is a bad design decision from the NES era that makes the game a bit unfair and not fun - it's another reason why you must play carefully instead of constantly running like in Contra and sometimes need to inch the screen forward bit by bit. I had a turret shoot me the minute I jumped on a moving platform in Stage 2 and I died from falling a pit. There are also Super Mario Bro's style firewhips that don't show up unless they are completely on your screen, making platforming more difficult than it needs to be. Also, you can only shoot forward and not in directions, which is problematic with some enemy types, but most of game seems built around it.
I got to stage 3 and I think the game is OK and gets better with trial and error vs pure skill.  I see $1 worth of content here, though I only recommend this to big fans of NES/NES style games.

LIMBO is... Bizarre
This is a title which divides opinion, on one hand it's artsy take on the 2D platformer genre, which is dark, disturbing and deeply emotive. But on the other side, it's bland, bleak and a very generic puzzler.
As a game, the atmosphere created is fascinating, it's on par with Amnesia. Forever alone is a phrase which springs to mind and it truly is the sole feeling throughout the game, and the noir feel supports and enhances this feeling. The mood is continued all the way through, but towards the end the core feel of the game shifts towards desperate survival rather than loneliness and this is emphasised by more intricate puzzles.
There two key elements to this game, puzzles and setting. This said, as a fan, a price of £5-£6 seems fair, but I would suggest that it could be picked up at close to £3-£4 and be more justified.

The controls are pretty basic, the physics is magnificent and the difficulty curve is just right. The best thing about the game would probably be that the puzzles you encounter dont require raw skill like in most platformers, but most of the times, if something you do doesn't work, you need to take a different approach. You will, nevertheless, die a lot, but the save points are so frequent that you will not be frustrated at all. Perhaps LIMBO's greatest shortcoming is its short duration, but its quality definitely makes up for it.

I saw the trailer for Jet Gunner sometime last year.
It looked like a fun Contra clone with a little twist but the trailer is very misleading.
What lies underneath the veneer of "Nestalgia" is a buggy ugly mess.
Having issues with my first time playing I looked tp the forums. It seems the game had gone through controller issues before that still haven't been rectified. At one time it had a flawed controller support, then no controller support at all, back to a flawed controller support.
My experience with this is the game not wanting to recognize my 360 controller's buttons, anything but the D+Pad/Stick did nothing.
My USB controller seemed to work fine other than the jump and fire buttons being opposite from each other and making speeding jumping and shooting gameplay a pain. Also the pause button isn't mapped to the controller in either case.
Granted this is an easy fix with one of the many keyboard to controller mapping programs out there but I'd rather not bother with that when a game should have that built in and working out of the box.
Lagging issues seem to be common. For me the culprit was the 360 controller. This cause the game to run super slow. Once it was removed and the game restarted it ran fine.
As for aesthetics and game design: One of the most jarring things upon starting the game the first time was the cut scene characters and title screen art. The character's faces were, as my nephew referred to them , "derpy". While the game play art didn't look that bad. The sprites are either two or three colors tops and sometimes they look like recognizable figures other time they look like unidentifiable shuffling blobs.
The levels are basic platforming fair while the enemy placement is erratic. It's as if the developer thought more baddies on screen = higher difficulty. Which doesn't work when they aren't programmed well or in a way where the player can learn from each pass through of the levels. On a few occasions a enemy on screen that was meant to be a tricky trap end up some where it didn't belong on screen. I also felt like there was no point in trying to take my time to fight enemy as they'll hit you regardless of anything you do. I made it through a level just booking it and using the "jet" to avoid danger and did better than actually fighting the enemies which is the "gunner" part of the game.
I had high hopes for Jet Gunner being I had it on my wishlist for so long but with the technical issues, ugly artwork, and questionable game design I can't suggest this game even with it's low price.

UnnyWorld shall be my second review for a Free-to-Play Steam title and I have to admit that this particular gameplay formula is starting to grow on me. It really proves those old adages, “Never say never” and “You won't know for sure until you've tried.” Perhaps I was more against the concept of gaming on a cramped smartphone screen than the games which debuted on the mobile platforms. This is Unnyhog’s Steam debut and they have successfully ported UnnyWorld from Android and iOS terminals.
Not much to spoil about the storyline since it’s fairly generic. A battle of Good against Evil, that somewhat stretches those definitions. Would raiding and conquering another planet, fit the description for the good guys? Are the defenders, truly the antagonists? My advice is to leave the moral qualms at the door and simply have fun in this MOBA (multiplayer online battle arena) which mixes mythological elements with pure fantasy while taking some aspects of the gameplay to a whole new level. What’s a kingdom to a galaxy-spanning empire? It certainly isn’t a reskin of yet another “Clash of Whatever”, so I definitely wasn’t bored by the change of scenery and simple yet effective themes.
UnnyWorld succeds in offering a new spin to an already saturated market for F2P strategy/base builder titles. Its cartoonishly disproportionate planets reminded me of a more light-hearted version for Planetary Annihilation. Setting up your defenses shall be just as important as training the preset avatars for the upcoming battles. Speaking of the playable characters, they represent a combination between fairies and anthropomorphic animals. Cute lions, wolves, panthers, foxes and so on. They're all adequate melee fighters which use spells as both support and when delivering a coup de grâce. I can only presume that as with most similar titles in this genre, players get to forge their own tales in real time and in tune with their own skills and lessons learned the hard way.
Same as with its mobile counterparts, the Steam version for UnnyWorld is powered by the Unity Engine. As expected, it ran maxed out and scaled perfectly to my monitor’s native resolution of 4K. Not a single frame rate drop in sight and plenty of visual effects during most of those heated arena fights. Nothing to complain about, really. This isn’t a video game which emphasizes on state of the art visuals, yet the assets are detailed enough and it features the stability which is required for MOBAs to be enjoyed at their maximum potential. What’s worse than lag, when it comes to multiplayer? A poorly motivated or unskilled team? Not the game’s fault, buddy.
Voice acting isn’t half-bad if only it didn’t draw inspirations from Simlish (the gibberish spoken in The Sims franchise). The rest of the sounds are lacking, not in originality but in sheer diversity. Soundtrack repeats itself incessantly and for a game in which some structure upgrades can take a lot to complete along with the inherent tendancy of the gameplay to rack up hours, you’d certainly expect a few more songs thrown in the mix. Fortunately, that can be fixed fairly easy and at any time by the developer.
When you won’t be busy fighting for planetary domination, you’ll need to focus on developing your ever expanding domain. An aggressive team will only get you so far, since you’re just as susceptible to invasions from human opponents. Former allies, perhaps? It’s important to join a guild and maybe form your own once you’ll have the necessary resources and gained sufficient experience. The tutorial section explains most gameplay aspects in rich detail, so you’re not cut loose into the wild without having a solid starting position and you also receive a decently-sized currency stash.
Speaking of which, there are three types of in-game valuables. Aqvium is the common medium of exchange and it’s represented by purple crystals which can be mined (generated on an hourly basis) and used for pretty much anything you build or upgrade. The next in line, are the Green Gems sporting a swirl symbol. These help speed things up, from spell progression to reducing building times. Last but not least, the UnnyCoins (a literal coin with a “U” symbol on it) are the more advanced type which are as rare as the spell scrolls you’ll be using them on. As you’d expect, the Gems are the type of microtransaction which encourages impatient players to spend real cash on this form of currency. It’s your choice what you do with your own money, just know that UnnyWorld can be enjoyed even without spending on it, unless you actually want everything here and now.
It’s important for a F2P to draw a clear line between paying customers and the playerbase which chose not to, without leaving either side feeling ignored or even worse, scammed. While avatar cosmetic changes have yet to be implemented, you can already spend copious amounts of Gems on new planetary skins which feature holiday themes, such as Halloween or Valentine's Day. It doesn’t affect the gameplay but it’s a welcome change from the standard Green Garden, default skin. I appreciated the fact that UnnyWorld isn’t Pay-to-Win and patience along with strategic thinking, will guarantee a hard earned victory in the end.
Unless you are part of a guild, the servers (clustered in either Asia, North America or Western Europe) will pick two random team mates for you to battle in the already classic 3v3 arenas. The perfect formula for fast matches and team work, the maps themselves feature sufficient terrain variation and even the optional objectives and power-ups, all ensure that you won’t get bored. Sometimes, it is recommened you allow your two squad mates to handle the opponents while you're making a beeline for the enemy HQ, since its destruction spells a straightforward triumph. Tower defence elements and AI-controlled minions do their part and assist during most battles.
Even if you’re only willing to test out this a newly released Steam version while you’re waiting for a new game to be released, you’ll soon learn that UnnyWorld is worth the time you’re investing. It’s a great example of a Free-to-Play in which you’re not forced to spend cash in order to advance and I sincerely hope that it’s dev team shall continue supporting their project while adding new features, characters and especially more sounds.

PC port runs like a dream (even well optimized for weaker computers), with the nice touch of a chromatic aberration slider (though this is one of the few games I think works well with CA, as it does fit the aesthetic of an analog TV or a VHS well, but it's nice to have the option to change the intensity/turn it off). The style of the game just oozes quality, with beautiful hand-drawn animation, catchy music that fits the 1930s era cartoon style the game emulates. The game chooses to run at 60fps, a creative liberty which does make the animation all at once not quite fit the aesthetic but also looks gorgeous with the added frames in motion and greatly helps the fluid gameplay.
It's challenging, but fair. The mechanics are completely solid and responsive, as well as the threats are well telegraphed, which helps that you never really feel it's the controls which make you die rather than your ability. The bosses are creative, memorable, and fun (all with multiple stages) and often are somewhat tasks of dealing with multiple threats at once. There's some platforming run-and-gun levels, and it may take some people used to Mario and the like to un-teach themselves to not jump on enemies heads, but those who were fans of Contra, Gunstar Heroes, etc., should immediately feel at home.
Seriously, this is a quality video game that perfectly encapsulates the addicting 'one more go' mentality, and the style, charm, solid mechanics, and fairness in the challenge all make it so instead of frustrating it often is addictingly fun. It truly feels like they hit the nail on the head to accomplish everything they wanted to with this title, and I fully recommend it.

Just finished this game, took me roughly 2.5 hours. What a wild ride! Stray Cat Crossing not only has amazing art and music, but also a story telling style that will get your heart racing and it will be on your mind even after you have finished the game.
At the first glance at this game, the store page screenshots show that the art style is very unique and eccentric. Having played the game I absolutely agree that the art style played a huge part in creating the atmosphere and immersion of the game. It's made with RPGMaker, however the loving care put into the art, as well as its detail and quality, make it hard to notice the engine at all.
The story is about a girl named Cat, that got lost. I really don't want to spoil anything by giving out details, as the story is a crucial part of this story, and emotionally impactful. I'll say that it's a story about memories and the past, kind of like To the Moon's themes. The way the story is implemented is quite outstanding, with different layers to getting to  "what actually happened". In the end the story is revealed bit by bit, with symbolism and twists of reality. It indeed is very thought provoking and I'm still thinking about the events that happened and what the story is trying to say. I absolutely love games/ shows/ anime that do this! What came to mind after playing was Spirited Away by Studio Ghibli, and after this thought occurred to me I looked up the developer's site and it's listed as one of the influences. So kudos to them for conveying the atmosphere right!
The game play is generally very smooth, involving puzzles and some chase scenes. I had a lot of fun with the puzzles, and the difficulty is about just right for a game heavily focusing on story - made me use my brain but didn't make me overly frustrated. The first 2 acts are great, the 3rd drags out but felt worth it. However a gripe I had was the speed of talking which is on the slow side and unskippable. The game froze sometimes after saving (thankfully after saving not before!) But looking at an FAQ unfortunately this is due to some problem with the RPGMaker engine, and will not be game breaking on most machines.
1. The chase scene seems hard at first but don't give up! It's actually quite short. You can only jump over the small holes.
2. The OST is free, included in the game files!
Stray Cat Crossing is a game with great storytelling, with a dark and creepy atmosphere. If you're looking for a thought provoking and emotionally impactful game, look no further! In addition the unique art style and soundtrack will draw you right in. I highly recommend this game - it's a steal at its asking price on Steam.

Stray Cat Crossing sits at a strange intersection of drama, adventure, and horror. The horror comes from being locked in small areas (typically a single floor of a house) with surrealist characters as your only companions, as well as FMV scenes that interrupt your actions with jumpscares. The characters you encounter are creepy and may antagonize you, but there are very few of them that impede your progress or can send you to the game over screen.
The narrative of Stray Cat Crossing starts out shallow at first. During the first two acts, it seems like the characters are strange for the sake of being strange and no explanations are given for their behaviour. Near the end of the second act is when things start to become deeper, but still very obscured. During the third act, essentially the last half of the game, the loose threads begin to join and form a unified whole. There is a sense of discovery when you find out the significance of a seemingly throwaway task in the earlier part of the game. I was pleased with the way the story came together at the end. It could have been easy to leave everything vague or unanswered in a game as surreal as Stray Cat Crossing, but the developers thankfully brought everything to a conclusion.
Pros:
-the pixel art is wildly original
-the soundtrack swaps between creepy ambience, pastoral guitar plucking, and dissonance as needed
-the full soundtrack is included in the base game!
-story comes to a satisfying conclusion with everything tied up nicely in a big bundle of feels
-different characters have distinct personalities and speech patterns
-about half the puzzles have nothing explaining how to complete them, yet are still intuitive
-the repetition and changing of rooms. Revisiting the same rooms multiple times and seeing how they change as I advanced made an entire level of just three rooms interesting
-I really liked the saving system. Very stylishly done.
-The brevity of the game makes it very easy to finish, and after discovering the secrets at the end, it is worthwhile to play through again to see the foreshadowing.
-Very unique experience. It is not easy to compare with other games
Cons:
-the song "Skin Tight" from the trailer is only as long as it is in the trailer. 0:51 is just not long enough.

Alaskafish Thinks:
Personally, I think this game is much like Call of Duty's World at War, but better. I say this because the maps it's map sizes are great, player count is great (even for an old game there's tons of 64 player server's still), and the over all point is not just shoot 'em up, and best of all, no hackers.
Unlike CoD, you don't just run about shooting and getting kill streaks, you need to think about your actions, plan your attacks. It's much more tatical. You'll die tons of times in the game, and you'll most likely have a hard time starting. But once you learn and play as a team member and doing objectives, it really fun. You'll feel like a your actually there. The only way to check how much ammo you have is if you pull the mag out, feel the weight and actually guess how many bullets are in. Plus the one chambered, sometimes it will be or not! The fact that you can die so quickly makes the game so you will get adrenaline rushes when you're behind enemy lines, and you hear the tank rolling slowly by...
Single Player:
The single player is okay. The story is that you fight as the Nazis against the Russians and then vice versa. It's very repetitive to be honest with you. Take the objective, defend it, attack, defend, attack, defend, you get the point. Some times you'll have a tank mission and that's fun, but over all, very repetitive. I mainly used it as a tutorial before I hopped online, which does justice. Since the HUD is VERY minimal, spotting enemies are somewhat difficult. That's why when I played the single player, I could learn how to spot the Nazis and the Russians. The AI is very bad as well, you tell them to go there, but they wont. Or the enemy will just walk up to you and then stop walking.
Over all, single player - 5/10
Multi Player:
This is the main reason for the game. That's why I think people gave this game a 76/100 on metacritic. People were mad that they got a game focusing on multiplayer, but in realility, the single player is just there for tutorial sakes. Online play is the best thing about this game. The unlocking of weapons and attachments (take note that there's very FEW) and the progressing in the level up screen feels not so rewarding, but that's not really the point. The  point is that  the classes are all balanced, and you will most likely get some sort of adrenaline rush 99% of the time, knowing that the enemy has something to counter you. It's also much harder than Single Player, yet much more fun. The maps are great sizes, voice chat lets you communicate on your squads tactics. The steam workshop gives many maps to play on, some being giant in size, others going for a more arcade shoot 'em up style. Re-player value isn't the biggest, unless you have a friend.
Over all, multiplayer - 8.5/10
Would I buy it? Yes.
I give it a 8/5/10.

Mind Spheres bills itself as a physics puzzle game; while I won't dispute that technically that's true, if you're looking for deep puzzling you may want to look elsewhere.  To me, I'd say this is more of a "physics manipulation game" (as if video games didn't already have enough unnecessary sub-genres).  But yeah, if we're not being pendantic then yes it's a physics puzzle game.
Having said that, what Mind Spheres lacks in puzzle difficulty it makes up for in charm, and I enjoyed the time I spent with it; I'd like to see this be the prelude to a more advanced and polished version.  There's a good progression of new gameplay mechanics, and each one is introduced in what I think is an excellent way: you put a new thing in front of the player in a way that they're forced to interact with it, and due to the level's design they'll immediately understand how it works once they do.
This is entirely a matter of personal preference, of course, but I like the aesthetics.  It's like, puzzles in space!  Glowing, rotating platforms with a tech theme?  Well, of course, that's what things in space look like!
The ball movement feels satisfying and realistic.  I mean, we're not talking Havok physics engine here, but this game doesn't need that.  For what this game is, the physics are entirely up to the task; and for a physics manipulation game, that's the one thing you absolutely
get right.
From a puzzle standpoint, the difficulty starts out where it should, at "tutorial-easy", and by the end of the game it's ramped all the way up to "very easy".  To put some precision on that statement: to be fair, I am relatively good at physics puzzle games, but I certainly didn't expect to complete levels 9 and 10 of the Eternal Loops section
on the first try.
Other than the difficulty level (which may not even be a drawback depending on your individual opinion...personally I'm not the kind of masochist where every game I play has to be "I Wanna Be The Super Meat Souls"), there are a few things to point out in the way of drawbacks.  The game is a big-time memory hog, and while I didn't have any stability issues as a result, one or two people in the forums reported it.  When you're rotating things around on the screen, they can behave pretty erratically; for a turn-based type game this isn't a showstopper, but it can be a bit aggravating sometimes when you're trying to place an object just so and it keeps spazzing out like a possessed fidget spinner.  There are a couple of times in the game where you're forced to trial-and-error because you can't scroll the screen up to see what's up there so you can predict trajectory (which is unfortunate for a game that's all about predicting trajectory).
All in all, the game is fun for what it is, the aesthetics are nice, the physics are on point, and the controls may make you roll your eyes a bit but the issues won't keep you from enjoying the game.  Mind Spheres is rough around the edges but it's more than the sum of its parts and at this "super-indie" price point it's definitely worth a quick play-through.

Day 27. Best I can figure, I'm somewhere North of Whitehorse in the Canadian Yukon.  It's only November but snow covers everything here.  My plane was brought down by some freak electrical storm that seems to have rendered anything with a charge inoperable. It's been hard these last couple weeks. The meager supplies I was able to scavenge after the crash that brought me here have run out.  I'm tired, cold, hungry and thirsty.... but alive.
I was able to bring down a deer a few days back but what meat that's left is starting to spoil.  I still hear the wolves so I know they're out there, watching me, waiting for their chance. I've killed a few of them but there's so many and my ammo is dangerously low. Why are they so intent on attacking me? Does it have something to do with that storm? I'm not as scared of them as I once was, my black fur coat is proof of that.  Although there is one.  I've only seen glimpses of him in the early morning and after sunset but I can tell he is bigger and smarter.  He seems to have taken a special interest in me, some vendetta perhaps.
Currently, I'm holed up in an abandoned cabin by a lake, frozen 1 meter thick. I feel like the walls are starting to close in on me a bit so take a chance and go out into the frigid wild. They sky is dark but calm.  It's two below freezing but I've grown used to that. I look first to the woods, checking for danger, and then set out onto the ice.  I haven't eaten today and I'm getting hungry so I head for a little fishing shack on the lake and chop my way through the frozen pond. Fishing for two hours produces some little guys that are barely worth cooking and one nice small mouth. Uh oh.. when I look up from the the fishing hole I notice it's gotten really, really cold. And not just snowing, complete whiteout blizzard. I build a fire to warm up a bit and cook my fish, eat them and wash them down with some fresh water from my pack.
I'm starting to feel tired but I'm too not worried.  It won't be my first night under the stars. I'll just set down my bedroll.... and then it hits me. I left the sleeping bag in the cabin! I was only going a hundred yards to fish and didn't think to bring it along. Without the warmth of the sleeping bag I'll freeze in my sleep and never wake up. Okay, I know I'm not far from the cabin so if I walk straight and follow the shore I'll run right into it. Except it's not there! I keep the shore on my left and start going around the lake. Getting colder.. And hungry again.. I feel my strength dropping fast. I head back to the middle of the lake to get back in the shack, see if I can get the fire going again. Blizzard still coming down and now it's dark. The wind is howling, cold flakes are burning my face. I light my lantern thinking it might put off a little heat but it hardly keeps my fingers warm.
Out of the rushing torrent of snow a dark shape steaks towards me.  It barely registers what is happening before I feel the fangs in my forearm. I fight him off with my knife but I'm hurt bad. I really need to find that shack, now! I tie on a quick bandage to stop the bleeding but I know I'm in trouble.  I'm tired, starving and freezing but I suffer on to where the shack should be. I see something up ahead, is it the shack?? Through the roar of the wind I make out the sounds of a second wail, this much more deadly and I know.  It's the Alpha I've seen near the train tracks.  The smell of blood must have been carried by the storm and brought him out of hiding.  He circles me slowly, sizing me up.  I know it and he knows it, there's nowhere to run.  I gather my remaining courage and charge the beast. The struggle is over almost as soon as it started. He gets his jaws around my throat and I fall. I'm still slightly conscious as he starts to feed.

Limbo is an enjoyable little platformer that mostly makes it on its striking monochromatic aesthetics. Despite being featureless, silent silhouettes, the well-animated characters enable a setting as rich as that found in any other game. The gameplay is not extra-ordinary - its just a typical platformer - but most of the puzzles are well done.  Unfortunately, later puzzles are less fun because they are too dependent on reflexes; I'm never sure if I have the wrong "solution" or if it is right but I'm just not fast enough. This results in a lot of trial and error (and error and error and error) gameplay; lots of frustrating repetition as I try to get that jump "just right". Worse, the end-game hardly justifies the effort.  While I "get" the eerie, open-to-interpretation plot, I'd rather all my effort be rewarded with a proper wrap-up to the game. Still, as a short (and cheap) alternative to the usual big-name games, I enjoyed my brief diversion into Limbo.
